date_note: Date is CERT.hr's publication day; the SMS campaign's start was not stated.
title: CERT.hr: fake SMS messages impersonating HZZO link to a banking trojan
summary: Croatia's CERT.hr reports fraudulent SMS messages that pose as HZZO and say the recipient's health insurance status has changed, urging them to check an official app via a shortened link. CERT.hr describes the app as an advanced banking trojan that steals passwords and multi-factor authentication codes. HZZO states it does not send these messages.
plain: Fake texts in Croatia claim to be from the health insurer and push an app that is a banking trojan stealing passwords and login codes.
exec: Customers' bank credentials and one-time codes are being targeted through a trusted public-body brand.
action: Do not open links in or reply to the messages and delete them. If the app was installed, disconnect the phone from the internet, tell your bank, change passwords from another device and report losses to the police (MUP), as CERT.hr advises.

key_findings: SMS imitates HZZO about a changed insurance status
Linked app is a banking trojan stealing passwords and MFA codes
recommendations: If installed, disconnect phone and tell your bank

validation.note: Single government CERT notice read (CERT.hr, 19 Nov).

review.note: date 19 Nov, SMS text, banking trojan wording, HZZO denial, advice match CERT.hr notice
